findings.text: tested_stamp excludes a stamp that has already been tested from every future pass, with no expiry, so one untrusted or non-moved verdict for stamp B is final for B: HEAD advances to B while a tracked file under reckon/ is dirty, the loop tests once at :2165-2167, records tested_stamp = B, and when the dirt is later discarded the identity is still B (source_code_identity reads only the committed HEAD tree, checkout_trust.py:363-382), so the supervisor keeps its stale image indefinitely; the same pin happens on a transient untrusted reason such as an import-probe timeout (checkout_trust.py:959-961) or a race in which the verdict's own identity read disagrees with code_stamp() and returns moved=False. This is a regression against 407e04e0ad, where the verdict was recomputed each pass and a tree that became trusted was adopted, and it defeats the section's purpose (the 73-minute stale-image outage the fragment records) for that stamp; the repository's owner of this pacing retries with a backoff instead of giving up (reckon/crew/follower_reload.py:333-343, 373-400). No gate arm covers it: tests/test_the_fleet_supervisor_runs_current_code.py:279-288 asserts only that a *different* stamp is tested once the interval passes.
